column4: The steady buzzing hum of an old red neon sign on a concrete wall at night: the high-voltage transformer's 50 hertz buzz with a faint irregular crackle and a soft flutter in the gas, heard from a couple of metres away outdoors, seamless, no music, no voices.
An old neon sign tube catching and stuttering: sharp electrical ticks and a buzzing that cuts in and out a few times, then holds steady. Close, outdoors at night, no music, no voices.
A heavy bowling ball rolling down a long wooden bowling lane: a deep rumbling roll growing louder as it goes, in a small concrete bowling hall, no pins hit at the end, no music, no voices.
A bowling ball smashing into all ten pins: a sharp explosive crash of hard wooden pins scattering and clattering into the pit behind, in a small concrete hall, close, no music, no voices.
A bowling ball hitting only a few pins: two or three hard wooden pins knocked over with a hollow clatter and rolling, in a small concrete hall, no music, no voices.

A bowling ball dropping into the gutter beside the lane and rolling along the channel with a hollow rumble, then a dull thud as it drops into the pit at the end, small concrete hall, no music, no voices.
A bowling ball coming back up the ball return: a rumble rolling under the floor, then a hard knock as it rolls out onto the rack against the other balls, close, no music, no voices.

The ambience of a small run-down bowling alley in a 1990s summer camp: balls rolling and pins crashing on other lanes now and then, a few people chatting and laughing in the distance, a fridge humming, seamless, no music, no clear words.
A small group of friends in a bowling alley cheering and clapping after a strike, one short whistle, no clear words, close, no music.
A few friends in a bowling alley groaning in disappointment after a bad throw, one laugh, no clear words, no music.
An old electric bell ringing briefly in a dark cramped machine room behind bowling lanes, a sharp metallic ring, a little echo, no music, no voices.
A heavy wooden bowling pin set down by hand upright on a wooden pin deck: one solid hollow knock, close, no music, no voices.
A pair of worn leather rental bowling shoes put down on a wooden counter: a soft double thud and the laces slapping, close, no music, no voices.
A short hiss of an aerosol disinfectant spray can sprayed into a shoe, close, no music, no voices.
The steady hum and faint electrical buzz of old fluorescent tube lights in a concrete hall, seamless, no music, no voices.
